recipes.name: Single Cup Hot Buttered Rum
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger dark Jamaican rum
2 tablespoons creme brulee flavored ice cream

steps.text: Combine butter, brown sugar, and confectioners' sugar in a large coffee mug; stir the mixture together with a fork until well combined. Pour in the rum, add the ice cream and cinnamon, and fill the remainder of the mug with simmering water. Mix the drink with the fork until the ice cream and butter have melted together to make a creamy topping. Sprinkle with a dash of nutmeg, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Single Cup Hot Buttered Rum
raw_recipe.description: When you're in the mood for a hot buttered rum, but you don't need enough for a group, make this one-mug recipe.

review.reviewBody: Several months ago before you posted this as a recipe, I asked if anyone had a Buttered Rum recipe in the exchange. You were kind enough to write the entire recipe out on my post. I tried it, I loved it and now I'm happy to see that I can rate it. I realized you posted it when I went to review your awesome shrimp salsa. Please WW, keep the recipes coming! :-)

I didnt have ice cream, so I just used whole milk with a little splash of vanilla instead of ice cream and water. I used cruzan black strap rum which is really really dark and it turned out good. it was pretty strong, but I think that's kind of the point of this drink
I am lactose intolerant and didn't have any ice cream so I added almond milk creamer instead. Then I heated up my almond milk instead of water. It was terrific.

This was exactly what I needed for this -37C weather! I used salted caramel ice cream (closest I could find) and Kracken rum since I had it on hand. Will definitely try again using hot coffee instead of hot water!

This is a superb recipe. I am now working on my second mug. Lacking the crème brûlée flavor, I tried mixing in a bit of powdered cocoa. Alternatively, as noted by Mark Bittman in his cookbook, when nothing else is at hand one can get the "brûlée" part by blasting some sugar with a propane torch until it bubbles and browns. Then, add cream and presto: the crème brûlée ice cream effect. Happy New Year!

This recipe lends itself to adjustments very well! I used what I had on hand: Captain Morgan Spiced Rum and frozen whipped cream instead of ice cream. Only used brown sugar, omitting the confectioners sugar. Two oz of rum :) So rich and creamy and delicious!! I was feeling icky but no longer after one of these!

Thank you for creating a 1 cup version of this! I needed to tweak this a bit due to refined sugar sensitivity. I subbed agave syrup for both the brown and confectioners sugar. I didn't have any nutmeg left after Thanksgiving, so I did without. All in all, IT WAS DELICIOUS. If I get around to tracking the exact way I make it next time, I'll let you know.
We didn’t have any ice cream on hand, so we substituted it with 2 tablespoons of heavy cream, and added a 1/4 teaspoon of vanilla.

Delish. I used Skinny Cow dulce le leche ice cream. The addition of the ice cream at the end cooled it down a little too much for me. I popped in the micro for 30 seconds and it was fine. I would suggest stirring up the ice cream before adding it to warm it a little.
This recipe is really good. I made it with vanilla ice cream and added an extra tablespoon. My husband liked it very much.
Yum, yum, yum!!! Love it. I used Captain Morgan's Spiced Rum and Vanilla Rum coffee creamer instead of icecream. It turned out fantastic, will definantly be making another one!!
Fantastic, really hit the spot on a cold winter evening. Only tweak was instead of cinnamon I hit the top with a dash of pumpkin pie spice. I'll look forward to this all winter long! Thank you
Yum! I changed the ice cream to pure whipping cream, because that was what I had on hand.
Made no changes except more icecream. Oh, and rum. May be the best hot buttered rum I've ever tasted, let alone made. Yay for the single serving!!
Hello, new winter fave! So good - and just the thing for a chilly day. Used vanilla bean ice cream and it was perfect!
Wow! Really good. Totally recommend!

This was SO yummy on a cold winter night! It was good to find a single version of this drink since I've only seen the ones that make a huge amount. I just doubled it, and it was perfect for a regular-sized mug. I used milk (for a nice and creamy result) and only used brown sugar (no confect), and it was the perfect sweetness. I highly recommend this!
too sweet for me and I didn't use the sugar or ice cream. won't make again.
Very good base, I changed things because I didn't quite have everything. I used coconut rum and vanilla ice cream then added a healthy splash each of Baileys and half and half. Yummo!
I added a little vanilla and used coconut rum.... so good!
